headline: Nvidia shares plunge 5% despite strong earnings beat
body:
Nvidia shares fell sharply Thursday, declining about 5%, even after the chip giant posted a fourth-quarter earnings and revenue beat. The decline puts the stock on pace for its worst day since April, as investor concerns around the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom dampened enthusiasm about its better-than-expected results.

Nvidia reported record revenue of $68.13 billion for the quarter, up 73% year-over-year, and adjusted earnings of $1.62 per share, exceeding analyst expectations of $1.53. The company generated a free cash flow of $35 billion in the quarter and $97 billion for fiscal year 2026.

However, the market is very much in 'prove it' mode, and Nvidia just didn't quite 'prove it' with these earnings, according to Tom Graff, Facet's chief investment officer. 'Nvidia is dealing with the cross section of high expectations priced into the stock, but also a skeptical market,' he said. 'That will probably make for a bumpy ride for at least the next couple of quarters.'

headline: J.M. Smucker shares surge 7.8% on strong coffee pricing strategy
body:
J.M. Smucker shares jumped 7.8% in pre-market trading Thursday after the food company reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results, boosted by strong performance in its coffee segment and effective price increases.

The company earned $2.38 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $2.34 billion, beating analyst expectations of $2.27 per share on revenue of $2.32 billion. The increase in comparable net sales reflects a 10 percentage point increase from net price realization, primarily driven by pricing actions taken to offset inflation and tariff impacts.

Smucker's third-quarter gross margin improved to 40.2% from 36.9% last year, and the company now expects annual adjusted earnings per share in the range of $9.85 to $10.15, compared with the prior forecast of $9.70 to $10.10. The company currently purchases approximately 500 million pounds of green coffee annually, with the majority coming from Brazil and Vietnam.

headline: Stellantis posts first annual loss in company history after $26.3 billion EV write-downs
body: Jeep maker Stellantis reported its first annual loss in company history, posting a net loss of $26.3 billion, or 22.3 billion euros, after taking massive write-downs due to electric vehicles and scaling back its EV strategy. The loss includes write-downs totaling 25.4 billion euros, as the company sharply scales back its electric vehicle strategy.

said Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa in a statement.

The writedowns - also caused by vehicle quality problems that Filosa attributed to cost-cutting under former boss Carlos Tavares - include about 6.5 billion euros in cash payments, expected to be spread across four years from 2026. The company now expects a preliminary net loss of between 19 billion and 21 billion euros in the second half of fiscal 2025 and won't pay a dividend this year.

headline: Copper miners rally as 'Dr. Copper' extends seven-month advance
body:
Copper futures, often called 'Dr. Copper' for their use in electronics and building materials and utility in gauging the health of the economy, rallied another 0.9% Wednesday, putting the metal on pace to advance for a seventh consecutive month in February. May contracts are ahead by a little more than 2% in February and are set to record their longest monthly advance since February 2011.

On the London Metal Exchange (LME), the 'red metal' climbed to a staggering $14,527 per metric ton in late January 2026, maintaining a steady altitude above the $13,000 mark as of February 25, 2026. So far in 2026, copper futures are higher by 6.4%.

Copper miners have benefited significantly from the rally. The $8 billion Global X Copper Miners ETF (COPX), a portfolio of 41 stocks, has gained 12% in February alone, over 30% year to date and more than 140% in the past 12 months. The strong performance reflects robust demand for copper in electric vehicles, renewable energy infrastructure, and data centers.

headline: Qnity shares jump 3.5% on strong earnings beat and transformation plan
body:
Shares of Qnity, the semiconductor technology company, jumped more than 3.5% after the company reported fourth-quarter results that significantly exceeded analyst expectations and announced a multi-year transformation initiative.

The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.82 for Q4, crushing the consensus forecast of $0.55 by 49%, while simultaneously announcing a multi-year transformation initiative targeting $100 million in annual cost savings through automation and artificial intelligence tools.

Qnity posted $729 million in 2025 net income and $1.4 billion in adjusted EBITDA, issuing 2026 sales and EPS guidance that exceeded expectations. The company also started a $500 million share buyback program. MSI wafer start data remains a good indicator for Qnity's overall demand, and the company continues to expect MSI to grow approximately mid-single digits this year.

headline: Lantheus shares slide 5% despite earnings beat, weak forward guidance
body:
Lantheus Holdings shares fell nearly 5% Thursday after the radiopharmaceutical firm issued lower-than-expected forward guidance for 2026, despite reporting fourth-quarter results that exceeded analyst expectations.

The company reported worldwide revenue of $406.8 million for the fourth quarter and $1.54 billion for the full year 2025, with GAAP fully diluted earnings per share of $0.82 and $3.41 for the fourth quarter and full year, respectively. Adjusted fully diluted earnings per share came in at $1.67 for the quarter, beating estimates by $0.51.

However, Lantheus expects full-year 2026 earnings in the range of $5 to $5.25 per share, with revenue in the range of $1.4 billion to $1.45 billion. This outlook fell short of analyst expectations of $5.51 in earnings per share, leading to the post-earnings decline despite the quarterly beat.
